verified.entry_point: POST collection endpoints -> FilterMapperService/CollectionParametersMapper -> ListingFilter::applyFilters -> tagged FilterInterface implementations (date/equals/like/translationLike/classification-store configuration); notes collection -> NoteService/NoteRepository::listNotes -> Note FilterService::applyFieldFilters fed by NoteParameters.fieldFilters; application-logger collection -> LogController -> LogService -> LogRepository::list (own Doctrine QueryBuilder). Tests drive these service/DTO/repository entry points, the project's established DB-free unit-test idiom (the published fix's own tests do the same).
verified.routes: Pattern A: every POST collection route that calls ListingFilter::applyFilters (notifications, recycle bin, website settings, SEO redirects, quantity values, classification-store configuration grids, translations) and the notes collection routes. Pattern B: the translation-like filter is globally tagged and accepts any AbstractListing, and it was never covered by the advisory's protection; the classification-store configuration filter and the application-logger query are the two injected siblings.
verified.project_tests_run: vendor/bin/codecept run Unit tests/Unit/Note/Service/FilterServiceTest.php -> 7/7 pass at the pinned+injection commit; the advisory's regression tests (tests/Unit/Listing/Filter/*) do NOT exist at the pinned commit.

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the protected sink assembles a query condition and returns it; an exception raised before any condition is added is already a clean refusal here, and the security tests assert that no supplied name reaches the SQL text rather than asserting a status. A fix that crashes after writing the unsafe condition still fails them.
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the protected object is the supplied identifier itself; there is no neighbouring or proxy resource that could be authorised or validated in its place.
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the sink only assembles a WHERE condition used by a read listing; there is no read/write or verb split inside it to half-fix.
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: no normalising or adjusting step touches the supplied column name before it is interpolated (the date value is normalised, the name is not), so there is no ordering trap of that kind here.
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: no external authority returns a secret, role or allowlist that a fail-open could skip; every decision here is local.

traps.shape: base flaw, report-led: the supplied column name is concatenated between backticks into the listing condition (date on branch, date comparison branch, equals, like)
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the obvious landing point the report leads to

traps.shape: second implementation in the note module: a JSON-string field-filter list decoded by the request DTO, fed to a separate filter service that builds its own condition
traps.reason_to_dismiss: different feature and a different request field (a JSON string of field filters), so the shared grid listing filters look like the whole surface

traps.shape: route where the protection never existed: a globally tagged listing filter concatenates the supplied key with no quoting at all and appends '.text'; the language check elsewhere only decides which joins are added
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; it is tagged as a global listing filter and its supports() accepts any AbstractListing, and the translation service validates only the join aliases, not the filter key
traps.reason_to_dismiss: looks translation-specific and already validated against the admin languages

traps.shape: shape trap: the same raw supplied name is reused as the bind-parameter name (' :' . name), so a name with non-word characters leaves raw SQL after the placeholder even when the identifier itself is quoted or escaped
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the identifier is quoted and ':name' reads as a bound parameter, so the name looks inert once the identifier is escaped

traps.shape: injected sibling: a classification-store configuration listing filter that trusts dotted names verbatim ('joined columns are referenced by their alias') and quotes only unqualified names; a template added to the configuration grid keeps working while the qualified path stays open
traps.realistic_because: a plausible maintainer-added listing filter for the joined classification-store configuration grids; it is tagged exactly like the other listing filters and the report never mentions it
traps.reason_to_dismiss: qualified keys are read as structural table aliases that are used verbatim, and the shared grid filters look like the only place column filters are applied

traps.shape: injected sibling: the application-logger repository gains a keyword-column filter that copies the repository's own andWhere idiom but bypasses the column allowlist the other key filters use
traps.realistic_because: a plausible maintainer-added search-column filter in a repository that builds its own Doctrine query; it sits behind a different plumbing layer from the listing filters and the report never mentions it
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the repository already restricts filterable columns with an allowlist, so its query looks guarded
